entry.title: Ep 18 – Discussing HIV With Your Doctor | Medicine Made General

media:group.media:title: Ep 18 – Discussing HIV With Your Doctor | Medicine Made General
media:group.media:description:
What is PrEP, who should consider it, and how do you talk to your doctor about HIV prevention? Ahead of World AIDS Day (December 1), Dr. Gail V. Berkenblit of Johns Hopkins joins “Medicine Made General” co-hosts Dr. Bimal Ashar and Katie Caviness for Episode 18.
In this episode, you’ll learn: • How pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) works • Other ways to prevent HIV • How to start these conversations with your care team
Listen to more episodes: https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/general-internal-medicine/podcast/episodes
NOTE: This podcast is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for medical advice. #HIV #PrEP #WorldAIDSDay

entry.title: Emergency Department Diagnosis of Concussion in Very Young Children with Head Injury

media:group.media:title: Emergency Department Diagnosis of Concussion in Very Young Children with Head Injury
media:group.media:description:
Jack Christian, a medical student at the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, discusses his recent publication, Emergency Department Diagnosis of Concussion in Very Young Children with Head Injury. Concussion research typically focuses on school-age children because they can explain the symptoms they are experiencing. However, toddlers ages 1–4 years old cannot explain what they are feeling. In this publication, the research team explains why concussions are underdiagnosed in this age group. #headinjury #johnshopkinschildrenscenter #pediatricconcussion #concussion https://www.hopkinschildrens.org/emergencymedicine

entry.title: Cal Ripken Jr. & Jim Palmer Step Up to the Plate for Prostate Cancer Awareness

media:group.media:title: Cal Ripken Jr. & Jim Palmer Step Up to the Plate for Prostate Cancer Awareness
media:group.media:description:
Hall of Famers Cal Ripken Jr. and Jim Palmer team up with Dr. Mohammad Allaf and the Johns Hopkins Brady Urological Institute to share an important message for men everywhere: Talk with your doctor about your prostate cancer risk and whether screening may be right for you. #prostatecancerawareness #johnshopkinsmedicine #prostatecancer
Just as these icons showed up on the field season after season, the Johns Hopkins Brady Urological Institute has provided patients with world-class urologic care for more than a century. Prostate cancer is the second-leading cause of cancer death among American men, but it’s also one of the most treatable cancers when caught early.
Don’t wait on the sidelines. Learn more about prostate cancer treatment at the Johns Hopkins Brady Urological Institute: https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/brady-urology-institute/conditions-and-treatments/prostate-cancer

entry.title: The Johns Hopkins Pharmacology Graduate Program

media:group.media:title: The Johns Hopkins Pharmacology Graduate Program
media:group.media:description:
The Johns Hopkins Department of Pharmacology and Molecular Sciences offers a multidisciplinary graduate program designed to prepare highly qualified individuals to be future leaders in academic and industrial biomedical research. The Pharmacology Graduate Program at the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine offers predoctoral training with a focus on chemical biology, the molecular interactions of living systems and the application of this knowledge to pharmacology. Students are encouraged to develop individually tailored programs of study to meet their particular research interests and career objectives. #Pharmacology #JohnsHopkins https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/pharmacology_molecular_sciences/

entry.title: Neuroretinal Layer Thinning on OCT Imaging and Hemoglobin A1c in Youth with Type 1 Diabetes

media:group.media:title: Neuroretinal Layer Thinning on OCT Imaging and Hemoglobin A1c in Youth with Type 1 Diabetes
media:group.media:description:
Risa Wolf, director of the Pediatric Diabetes Program at Johns Hopkins Children’s Center, discusses her latest research with the Wilmer Eye Institute, Johns Hopkins Medicine, titled “Neuroretinal Layer Thinning on OCT Imaging and Hemoglobin A1c in Youth with Type 1 Diabetes.” The objective of this study was to determine if retinal layer thickness changes on optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging were associated with glycemic outcomes and diabetic retinopathy in youth with type 1 diabetes. To learn more about this publication, visit: jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaophthalmology/fullarticle/2850931 #pediatricdiabetes #johnshopkinsmedicine #opticalcoherencetomography #referral
